title: Singers with megaphones and the Piron band's vocalist
summary: Early bands had no featured vocalists, only members singing through megaphones; Joe recalls hearing Piron's band with a singer on a carnival night around 1924.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Let me ask you this. In any of these early bands that you saw, Toots Johnson, the Banner Band, Martel, did anybody in the band sing, or...
Oh, yes! The drummer more or less... In Toots Johnson's band, a guy named Boosta(?) used to have one

of those megaphones. He would sing. And Tody Harris, that band... And Tody didn't play nothing. He didn't even play a note! But he was still out in front of that band. And he had his megaphone. He sang. And I think Gustan... Gustan played a trombone. And I think all them bands had these megaphones.
So in other words, there was no featured vocalist with the band. Just the band members would sing.

That's right. None of them had a vocalist that I know of. I think in 1924, I seen...the Piron Band in New Orleans had a girl singing with them. I can't remember. I believe it was either a girl, or some guy who was doing a vocal on "I Wonder What's Become Of Sally." Just come out. About 1924. [SINGS]... "I won-der what be-come of Sally."
If it was a girl, it might have been...
I know it was somebody singing with that band.
Esther Bidoux(?) or Lilah(?) Bolden were the singers who recorded with Piron.
It well could have been, but it was a carnival night, and I had been drinking, and we stopped near the St. Catherine Hall, and Piron was playing. And
that ...(?)... had pretty arrangements. There was a back-up (?) at the time.

That's interesting, because the first time I've ever heard of a featured vocalist with a band is you mentioning that Piron had one. In practically all the New Orleans bands, the early bands, they've never seemed to mention anything about featured vocalists or girl singers...

Never seen one outside the Piron band. It was the first one... Now, it could have been a girl. But I remember it was such a pretty vocal and a pretty tune. That tune also came out as a waltz. [SINGS] "I wonder what's become of Sally, that old gal of mine..." And then after we learned it, we'd pick it up and play it in double time.
